# KM-150 — Integration: agent joins and chats on the local stack

**Lane:** acceptance · **Complexity:** 3 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KM-130, KM-133, KM-134, KM-135, KM-143, KM-144, KM-147 · **Serializes with:** none
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `packages/agent/src/mcp/main.ts` (the default export's client factory only; KM-144 created the file), `packages/agent/src/mcp/wiring.ts`, `packages/agent/src/mcp/wiring.test.ts`, `tests/integration/agent/agent-join-chat.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/agent/mcp-stdio.ts`. Never `packages/agent/bin/khala.mjs` (KM-103 owns it; contracts C12).

## Outcome

The real `khala mcp` process joins a channel on the long-lived local stack. A headless owner confirms it in the browser; the agent reads the three messages sent before it joined (AE1), receives a live human message into its inbox, and sends a reply. The other human's browser shows that reply attributed to the agent. One Playwright spec proves this end to end through the actual stdio MCP binary.

## Context and evidence

- Plan U12 integration scenario: "with the U1 stack and a U11-driven browser, the agent joins, reads full history, sends, and the browser sees it". The live-agent gate is in the Verification Contract. Requirements R4, R5, R6, R8, R11; AE1, AE4.
- KTD3 sequence (plan "High-Level Technical Design"): agent POST join → owner confirms → agent polls credentials → crypto and cross-signing → ready → browser `client.invite` (MSC4268 bundle) → agent `joinRoom`.
- Reusable human fixtures at `5db209cc`:
  - `tests/integration/human/fixtures.ts:75`: `readLiveHumanEnvironment`.
  - `fixtures.ts:120`: `signIn`.
  - `fixtures.ts:131`: `freshPage`.
- Proven selectors in `tests/integration/human/create-share-chat.spec.ts`:
  - `:107-109`: create channel (`'Create channel'`, `'Channel name (optional)'`).
  - `:112-114`: send (`getByLabel('Message',{exact:true})`, `'Send message'`, `.timeline__row:not(.timeline__row--pending)`).
  - `:117-120`: copy link (`'Copy my channel link'`, clipboard).
  - `:126-130`: join (`"You're in."`, `.join-joined__room-id`).
  - `:140`: `'Open channel'`.
- `tests/integration/playwright.config.ts:3-11`: specs need `KHALA_E2E_LIVE=1` and `KHALA_E2E_DISPOSABLE_ENV`, and optionally `KHALA_E2E_CERT_SPKI`. The config's `testDir: '.'` (`:13`) picks up `tests/integration/agent/*.spec.ts` automatically.
- The local gateway is self-signed for `IP:127.0.0.1` (`infra/preview/external-local.mjs:109-114`, which KM-101 lifts into `infra/local/stack.mjs`). The Node agent process therefore needs `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` pointing at that certificate under `.khala-local/certs/`.
- **Live tests are not unit tests (reconciliation A10).** This spec is a Playwright `*.spec.ts` that runs only via `pnpm test:integration` (root `package.json:18` at `5db209cc`), never via any package's default `test`. If you add any vitest live test (for example in `packages/agent`), name it `*.live.test.ts`; it is excluded from that package's default `test` script and runs only via `test:live` (KM-110 set this up for `packages/agent`).
- The agent package is `@khala/agent` (bin `khala`), run from TypeScript source via `tsx` (contracts C1).

## Scope

1. Wire `khala mcp` to `createKhalaAgentClient` (KM-143) by replacing KM-144's placeholder factory inside the C12 default export of `src/mcp/main.ts`. The bin is untouched.
2. Wire the KM-147 Codex waker into the MCP process for Codex sessions (Round 2 R7; moved here from KM-151, which now only verifies it live).
3. A minimal stdio JSON-RPC client helper for tests.
4. One live Playwright spec covering join, history, live intake, own-sender filter, send and browser attribution.

## Contract and invariants

contracts.md C10 (verbatim):
> - Commands: `pnpm stack:up | stack:down [--wipe] | stack:logs [service] | stack:status`.
> - State lives in `.khala-local/` (git-ignored): `state.json`, `logs/<service>.log`, `certs/`.
> - `state.json` always includes `secrets.registrationSharedSecret`, `secrets.passwordDerivationSecret` and the Dex user credentials (`users: [{ email, password }]`). Live tests read them from there; KM-101 may add fields but never removes these.
> - `stack:status` prints JSON: `{ origin, homeserver, dex, users: [{ email, password }], services: { synapse, postgres, dex, netlify, gateway } }`. Each service maps to `up` or `down`.

C2 confirm page and handshake (excerpt, verbatim):
> - **Confirm URL.** The `confirmUrl` is `<app origin>/agent/confirm?joinId=<joinId>`.
>
> `// GET  /api/human/agent-join/status?joinId=<joinId>   → 200 AgentJoinView   (browser polls every 1s until state === 'ready')`

C3 (verbatim excerpt; KM-135 renders it):
> ```ts
> export type Participant =
>   | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'human' }
>   | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'agent'; ownerLabel: string; harness: Harness }
>   | { matrixUserId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'unknown' };   // an unknown member never fails the whole response
> ```

C7 tools are as quoted in KM-144. C5 inbox lines are `InboxEntry`.

C12 (verbatim excerpt):

```ts
// packages/agent/src/mcp/main.ts (KM-144 creates it; KM-150 wires the real client and the Codex waker into it)
export default async function main(argv: readonly string[]): Promise<number>;
```

Invariants checked by the spec:
- I1. The agent's own sent text never appears in `<XDG_STATE_HOME>/khala/claude/<sessionId>/inbox.jsonl` (AE4 / R11).
- I2. The stack is not torn down by the spec (R14). The spec creates its own channel and leaves it. The *operator of the run* wipes and restarts the stack before each run (Verification), because each Dex user must sign in from its first-ever browser device for MSC4268 history sharing to work.
- I3. The spec output never prints `accessToken` or `pollSecret`. Read `session.json` only to assert that it exists.

## Implementation pointers (refreshable @ 5db209cc)

### Files

- Create `packages/agent/src/mcp/wiring.ts`, exporting `createRealClientFactory(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, deps?: { createClient?: typeof createKhalaAgentClient; createWaker?: typeof createCodexWaker }): ClientFactory` (`ClientFactory` from KM-144's `main.ts`):
  - harness `claude`: `createKhalaAgentClient({ harness, sessionId, env })`. Claude needs no waker: its KM-146 watcher polls the inbox.
  - harness `codex`: create one `waker = createCodexWaker({ files: sessionFiles('codex', sessionId, env), threadId: sessionId })` per client; pass `onInboxAppend: () => waker.notify()` to `createKhalaAgentClient`; return the client wrapped so that `close()` runs `await client.close()` and then `await waker.stop()` (the other methods delegate unchanged, including `sendChannelEvent` when present).
- Modify `packages/agent/src/mcp/main.ts`, default export only. It becomes:
  ```ts
  export default async function main(argv: readonly string[]): Promise<number> {
    const stop = new AbortController();
    const onSignal = () => stop.abort();
    process.once('SIGTERM', onSignal); process.once('SIGINT', onSignal);
    try { return await runMcpCommand(argv, { createClient: createRealClientFactory(process.env), signal: stop.signal }); }
    finally { process.off('SIGTERM', onSignal); process.off('SIGINT', onSignal); }
  }
  ```
  A harness that stops its MCP server with SIGTERM instead of closing stdin then still reaches KM-144's I6 path (`runMcpServer` resolves on abort, every client `close()`s, and KM-143's `close()` removes `session.json`, as C5 requires). Keep `createPlaceholderClient` and `runMcpCommand` unchanged: KM-144's `main.test.ts` uses them.
- Create `packages/agent/src/mcp/wiring.test.ts` (unit, fakes only):
  1. Codex: the factory creates exactly one waker per session id with `threadId === sessionId`; an `onInboxAppend` call reaches `waker.notify()`; `close()` calls `client.close()` and then `waker.stop()`, in that order.
  2. Claude: no waker is created, and `onInboxAppend` is not passed.
  3. Signal path (the default export itself is not unit-tested; it only wires): `runMcpCommand(['--harness','codex'], { createClient: <fake factory>, input: <idle PassThrough>, output, signal })`, make one `tools/call` so a client exists, then abort `signal` → resolves 0 and that client's `close()` ran once.
- Create `tests/integration/agent/mcp-stdio.ts`. It exports `startMcp({ env }): { call(name, args): Promise<{structuredContent, isError?}>; close(): Promise<void> }`. It spawns `process.execPath` with `[<repo>/packages/agent/bin/khala.mjs, 'mcp', '--harness', 'claude']` and `stdio: ['pipe','pipe','inherit']`, sends `initialize` once, and matches responses by numeric id.
- Create `tests/integration/agent/agent-join-chat.spec.ts`.

### Worked example

The agent's view after the join (the `khala_read` `structuredContent`, abbreviated):
```json
{ "messages": [
  { "eventId": "$a", "sender": "@khala_…:khala.local", "senderKind": "human", "kind": "message", "body": "hist-1-<uuid>" },
  { "eventId": "$b", "sender": "@khala_…:khala.local", "senderKind": "human", "kind": "message", "body": "hist-2-<uuid>" },
  { "eventId": "$c", "sender": "@khala_…:khala.local", "senderKind": "human", "kind": "message", "body": "hist-3-<uuid>" } ] }
```
Bob's browser after the agent sends `agent-reply-<uuid>` shows a `.timeline__row` containing that text plus the agent label `Agent · <owner first name>`, for a join label of `Agent`, rendered by KM-135.

### Steps

1. Write `wiring.ts` and its test, then switch `main.ts`'s default export to it (Files, first three bullets). Run `pnpm --filter ./packages/agent test`. Smoke-test with the KM-144 smoke command; `tools/list` must still list the C7 tools (4, or 5 including `khala_event` if KM-173 has merged).
2. Write `mcp-stdio.ts` per the Files list. Reject a pending call after 60 s with `mcp_timeout:<tool>`.
3. Write the spec as one `test(...)` with `test.setTimeout(300_000)`:
   1. `environment = readLiveHumanEnvironment()`. Create `aliceContext` and `bobContext` with `browser.newContext()` (Playwright `browser` fixture).
   2. **Alice:** `alice = await freshPage(aliceContext, environment)` → `await signIn(alice, environment, environment.users[0])` → create a channel named `Agent ${environment.environmentId}` (`create-share-chat.spec.ts:107-110`) → copy the link (the clipboard pattern at `create-share-chat.spec.ts:116-120`).
   3. **Bob:** `bob = await bobContext.newPage()` → `bob.goto(link, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })` → `signIn(bob, environment, environment.users[1])` → "You're in." → `Open channel` (`create-share-chat.spec.ts:126-141`).
   4. Alice sends `hist-1/2/3-<uuid>` and waits for each non-pending row. Bob joined before these messages, so he holds their keys.
   5. Start the agent:
      - `XDG_STATE_HOME = mkdtemp(os.tmpdir()/khala-agent-)`;
      - `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID = 'km150-' + uuid`;
      - `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` = `<repo>/.khala-local/certs/tls.crt` (KM-101 exports it in `.khala-local/e2e.env`; fail with a clear message if the file is absent);
      - `startMcp({ env: { ...process.env, ...those } })`.
   6. `khala_join {link, label:'Agent'}` → expect `structuredContent.state === 'awaiting_confirmation'` and a `confirmUrl` equal to `environment.appOrigin + '/agent/confirm?joinId=' + <joinId>` (assert the prefix `environment.appOrigin + '/agent/confirm?joinId='`).
   7. **Bob, as owner** (AE1: A2 confirms its agent): `bob.goto(confirmUrl)`, then click `getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm' })`. Keep the page open: it polls status and invites (KM-134 states: connecting "Connecting Agent… Keep this tab open.", done "Agent joined <channel>."). Also expect the done text `/Agent joined/` within 120 s.
   8. Poll `khala_status` every 2 s for up to 120 s until `state === 'connected'`, then assert that `agentUserId` matches `/^@agent-[0-9a-f]{8}-[a-z0-9]{6}:/`.
   9. **AE1:** call `khala_read {limit:30}` and assert that the bodies contain `hist-1`, `hist-2` and `hist-3`, in that order. History keys arrive asynchronously after the join (KM-110 retries for up to 15 s), so retry the read every 2 s for up to 30 s while any of them is missing (C11: `history()` omits events that stay undecryptable, so a missing body is the only symptom).
   10. **Live intake:** Alice sends `live-<uuid>`. Poll `inbox.jsonl` for up to 30 s until a line has that body, with `senderKind:'human'`.
   11. **Send:** `khala_send {text:'agent-reply-<uuid>'}` → `eventId` matching `/^\$/`.
   12. **I1:** wait 5 s, then assert that no `inbox.jsonl` line has `body === 'agent-reply-…'` or `sender === agentUserId`.
   13. **Bob's view:** go to the channel URL and expect a `.timeline__row:not(.timeline__row--pending)` containing `agent-reply-<uuid>` within 30 s. That row also contains the author `Agent · ` and the KM-135 badge text `Claude Code agent`. This attribution assertion is unconditional (KM-135 is a dependency). If KM-135 merged a different badge text, use the one in its component test.
   14. **Reload:** reload both pages and confirm both see `agent-reply-<uuid>`. Bob sees `hist-1..3` because he joined before them.
   15. `finally`: `mcp.close()` (stdin end; the process must exit within 10 s), close the contexts, and remove the temp dir. Then assert that `session.json` is gone after exit (C5 "deleted on process exit").

## Test scenarios

`tests/integration/agent/agent-join-chat.spec.ts`:
1. Join handshake through the real MCP binary → `awaiting_confirmation`, then `connected` after the owner confirms.
2. Covers AE1: the agent reads three messages sent before its join.
3. Live human message → one inbox line with `senderKind:'human'`.
4. Covers AE4: the agent's own message is absent from the inbox.
5. Agent send → visible and attributed in the other human's browser, and present after a reload.
6. Process exit → `session.json` deleted.

`packages/agent/src/mcp/wiring.test.ts` (unit; runs in the default `test`): scenarios 1–2 under Files.

## Verification

```sh
pnpm --filter @khala/agent test            # unit tests only; *.live.test.ts is excluded
pnpm typecheck
# Every live run starts from a fresh stack (Executor ruling): history sharing works only from a
# human's FIRST browser device, because the cross-signing bootstrap without UIA succeeds once per
# Matrix user. --wipe gives fresh Synapse users; down/up also rebuilds the web app and functions.
pnpm stack:down --wipe && pnpm stack:up && pnpm stack:status   # every service "up"
set -a; . ./.khala-local/e2e.env; set +a   # KM-101: KHALA_E2E_LIVE, KHALA_E2E_DISPOSABLE_ENV, users, KHALA_E2E_CERT_SPKI, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (KHALA_E2E_LIVE=1 alone is not enough)
pnpm test:integration tests/integration/agent/agent-join-chat.spec.ts
pnpm stack:status                           # still "up" afterwards (R14)
```
Done means the spec passes on two consecutive runs, **each** preceded by the `stack:down --wipe && stack:up` and `e2e.env` lines above (a second run on the same stack is expected to fail AE1: Alice and Bob would sign in from new devices). Attach the `pnpm stack:logs control` tail to the PR only on failure.

## Risks and stop conditions

- On a failure, look first at `pnpm stack:logs <service>`. If the cause is in another ticket's surface (join routes, confirm page, session crypto, history bundle), stop and report it to the Executor with the log excerpt; do not patch it here.
- **Stop** if the agent joins but `khala_read` lacks the history. That means MSC4268 did not hand over keys (check KM-130 cross-signing and KM-110 evidence). It is a settled-decision risk (KTD1/KTD4) and must be reported, not worked around.
- **Stop** if `.khala-local/e2e.env` or `.khala-local/descriptor.json` is missing after `pnpm stack:up`. That is a KM-101 gap.
- **Stop** if the reply renders without the KM-135 agent attribution. That is a KM-135 or KM-122 defect; report it, do not skip the assertion.
- **Stop** if `node packages/agent/bin/khala.mjs mcp` does not reach `main.ts`'s default export (KM-103's bin does not match C12). Report it; do not edit the bin.
- The confirm button name `Confirm` comes from plan U11. If KM-134 used another accessible name, use KM-134's, and note it in the PR.

## Complexity rationale

3: the first end-to-end path across seven merged tickets and a live stack. The code is small (the factory, plus the Codex waker wiring moved here by Round 2 R7), but the diagnosis is cross-component.
